nodes.label: Asymmetric Masking Design
nodes.rationale: Only REQUEST bodies are masked (outbound to Anthropic). System field and assistant prose are skipped intentionally: masking distorts model directives and assistant output carries no original user PII. tool_use inputs are masked because they may contain user-authored text verbatim (e.g. new_string in Edit).

nodes.label: System Reminder Preservation
nodes.rationale: <system-reminder> blocks in user messages contain trusted machine-generated content (skills list, CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md) injected by Claude Code harness — not user-authored PII. NLP models incorrectly flag these (e.g. 'Claude' as PERSON, dates, IPs). They are passed through unchanged to avoid breaking session context.

nodes.label: Person Allowlist False Positive Filter
nodes.rationale: Product names like 'Claude' are misclassified as PERSON entities by spaCy NER. An allowlist filters these before anonymization to prevent over-masking of legitimate product-name content in user messages.

nodes.label: Symlink-Safe Flag Write Design
nodes.rationale: Flag files (.caveman-active) are predictable paths. An attacker with write access to ~/.claude/ could replace them with symlinks pointing to ~/.ssh/id_rsa. safeWriteFlag uses O_NOFOLLOW, atomic temp+rename, 0600 permissions, and ownership checks on symlinked parent dirs to prevent symlink clobber attacks. readFlag enforces same protections plus a 64-byte size cap to prevent exfil of secret files via flag readers.

nodes.label: Graphify Full Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Multi-step pipeline (detect→extract→build→cluster→label→visualize) chosen so each stage is independently cacheable and incremental updates only re-run changed steps, saving tokens.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction via Subagents
nodes.rationale: Subagent dispatch pattern chosen over sequential file reading because it is 5-10x faster; each agent chunk processes 20-25 files in parallel, reducing wall-clock time to ~45s per batch regardless of corpus size.

nodes.label: Direct LLM Backend (Kimi/Ollama)
nodes.rationale: Kimi K2.6 and Ollama backends bypass Claude subagent dispatch entirely — 3x cheaper and avoids subagent overhead. Falls back to Claude subagents when no direct backend is configured.

nodes.label: Circular Dependency Detection Algorithm
nodes.rationale: DFS-based visited-set algorithm prevents infinite loops in skill dependency graphs; errors include the full path so the developer can see where the cycle occurs.

nodes.label: Hybrid Output Pattern (JSON + TOON)
nodes.rationale: TOON is always additive — JSON remains present for backward compatibility. TOON only generated for arrays >= 5 elements where savings justify overhead (25%+). This zero-breaking-change approach lets consumers opt-in without migration.

nodes.label: Karpathy Compoundable Wiki Pattern
nodes.rationale: Raw sources remain immutable; wiki pages are synthesized summaries. This separation means the wiki compounds over time (each ingest adds knowledge without destroying prior synthesis) and sources can be re-ingested safely.
